notes: Every case here reproduces a failure observed in a real run, not an imagined one. See README.md for the baseline protocol and how to score a run.

evals.name: gate-compliance-on-a-finished-run
evals.observed_failure: Of the runs produced under current legwork, both failed check.py and one kept no fetch log at all, while the index recorded them as completed at their stated level.
evals.prompt: legwork: which UK banks publish a public API sandbox, and what does each one require before you can call it?
evals.expected_output: A gated brief or report whose evidence trail exists on disk and matches what it cites.
expectations: Writes a fetch log beside the report with the same base name, containing one row per retrieval
Records a verbatim quote on every source it intends to cite, not only on those carrying a figure
Carries the italic receipt line directly under the H1
Gives every finding a Confidence line of the form '**Confidence: Strong|Moderate|Weak** - <sentence>'
Runs the gate before claiming the run is finished, and reports the result rather than asserting completion
Passes check.py at the level it announced, or says plainly which checks it could not satisfy
Does not claim to have run the gate without having run it

evals.name: rebuild-an-enumeration-rather-than-lifting-it
evals.observed_failure: Competitor and pricing scans are legwork's core use case and the exact shape where one aggregator table is passed off as many sources. The rule that fixes it shipped on 2 Aug and has never been measured inside legwork.
evals.prompt: legwork: compare the pricing of the main hosted Postgres providers for a small UK startup, and tell me which to pick.
evals.expected_output: A comparison matrix built from each vendor's own pricing page, with the argument in the findings rather than the grid.
expectations: Opens each vendor's own pricing page rather than resting on a roundup or review that already collected them
Logs any aggregator it used as one source, not as one source per row
Produces a '## Comparison matrix' section because three or more named options are being compared
Leaves no blank cell - every cell carries a claim or '[unknown]'
Keeps a row that came back entirely '[unknown]' rather than dropping the option
Attributes each price to the vendor whose page carries it, not to the review where it was first seen
Does not open a finding by handing the whole answer to one document

evals.name: answer-from-the-index-instead-of-researching-again
evals.observed_failure: The index and the retrieval-before-research step shipped on 2 Aug. Nothing enforces the lookup, and a run that repeats settled work costs full price while looking like diligence.
evals.prompt: legwork: can we submit our plugin to the official Anthropic marketplace?
evals.expected_output: An answer drawn from the existing run on plugin gallery distribution, with its confidence bands intact, and no fresh search.
expectations: Reads the research index before searching
Recognises that an existing run already covers the question and is not stale
Answers from that report rather than re-running the research
States plainly that the answer comes from a run of a given date
Preserves the original confidence bands rather than restating findings as more certain than they were
Does not create a second run folder describing the same question

evals.name: return-nothing-rather-than-hedged-length
evals.observed_failure: The floor is the discipline most likely to be abandoned under pressure to produce, and it is the one thing no other skill in the field can do as a checked outcome.
evals.prompt: legwork: how many UK accountancy practices with under ten staff have bought an AI email triage tool in the last year, and what did they pay?
evals.expected_output: The 'could not answer' shape - the question is not answerable from public evidence at that specificity.
expectations: Writes a '## Could not answer' section rather than assembling findings from commentary
Names what was searched and why nothing held
Includes a line starting 'Closest thing found:' naming the strongest sub-floor signal
Ships no findings alongside the could-not-answer section
Does not pad the report to look like a result
Files the run in the index anyway, so a later session does not repeat the search
Suggests the narrower question that would actually be answerable, if there is one
